questions.question: Describe the haematological changes during pregnancy. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the haematological changes during pregnancy [U]/[CO1]
  • ● Blood volume: Increases by 30–50%.
  • ● Physiological anaemia: Plasma volume increases more than RBC mass.
  • ● RBC production: Increases, with higher iron, folic acid and vitamin B12 requirements.
  • ● WBC and platelets: WBC count increases; platelet count may decrease slightly.
  • ● Blood coagulation: Clotting factors increase, raising the risk of thrombosis.(1 mark for
  • each point)

questions.question: Explain how Breast milk is expressed with a Breast Pump / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how Breast milk is expressed with a Breast Pump.[U]/[CO3]
  • Steps:
  • ● Wash hands: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water and ensure the breast pump
  • and its parts are clean.
  • ● Prepare the breast: Sit comfortably and gently massage the breasts to stimulate milk
  • flow.
  • ● Position the pump: Place the breast shield over the nipple, ensuring the nipple is
  • centred.
  • ● Express the milk: Switch on the electric pump or operate the manual pump. Start with
  • gentle suction and gradually increase to a comfortable level until milk flows.
  • ● Collect and store: Express milk from both breasts, pour it into a clean, sterile container,
  • label it with the date and time, and store it safely according to breast milk storage
  • guidelines. (5 mark)

questions.question: Explain how gastrointestinal changes help meet the nutritional demands of pregnancy. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how gastrointestinal changes help meet the nutritional demands of
  • pregnancy[An]/[CO1]
  • ● Decreased gastrointestinal motility: Progesterone slows intestinal movement, allowing
  • more time for nutrient and water absorption.
  • ● Nausea and vomiting: Hormonal changes, mainly increased hCG and estrogen, may
  • affect food intake, especially during the first trimester.
  • ● Heartburn: Relaxation of the lower oesophageal sphincter causes acid reflux.
  • ● Constipation: Reduced intestinal motility and increased water absorption cause
  • constipation.
  • ● Increased appetite: Higher energy and nutrient requirements support fetal growth and
  • maternal health.
  • ● Displacement of stomach and intestines: The enlarging uterus compresses the digestive
  • organs, causing early fullness and reduced meal capacity. (1 mark for each point)

questions.question: Compare and contrast the causes, symptoms, prevention, and health consequences of common nutritional deficiencies in women of reproductive age. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • Compare and contract the causes,symptoms,prevention and health consequences of common nutritional deficiencies in women of reproductive age.[An]/[CO2] (2 mark for each point) Deficiency Causes Symptoms Prevention Health Consequences Iron Poor intake, menstrual blood loss, increased requirements. Fatigue, weakness, pallor, breathlessness. Iron-rich foods, vitamin C, iron supplements. Anaemia, preterm birth, low birth weight. Folic acid Low intake of folate-rich foods, increased pregnancy requirements. Fatigue, weakness, megaloblastic anaemia. Green leafy vegetables, legumes, folic acid supplements. Neural tube defects, poor fetal development. Calcium Inadequate intake, poor absorption. Muscle cramps, weak bones, numbness. Milk, curd, ragi, green leafy vegetables, supplements if needed. Reduced bone strength, poor fetal bone development. Vitamin D Inadequate sunlight exposure, poor dietary intake. Bone pain, muscle weakness, fatigue. Sunlight exposure, fatty fish, fortified foods, supplements if needed. Poor fetal bone development, maternal bone problems. Vitamin B12 Low intake of animal foods, poor absorption.
